headline: Hot PPI couldn't buy the October hike back: wholesale prices ran +1.3% — the biggest jump since March 2022 — and the market still faded October to ~29%, because the AI risk-off owned the tape. The 10-year collapsed ~27bp off the CPI-day spike to a three-week low, the dollar fell against every G10 currency except the aussie, gold reclaimed ~$4,150+, and the franc — not the yen — was the haven that finally showed up. Warsh speaks 10:30pm CT, the last Fed voice before Saturday's blackout.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: PPI blew past expectations (+1.3%, biggest since March 2022) and the market ignored it: October odds fell to ~29%, the 10-year collapsed ~27bp off the CPI-day spike, and DXY faded to ~102.05.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the wholesale print came back hotter than the consensus on every line — headline +1.3% m/m vs 0.6% expected (y/y 6.3% vs 5.5%), core +0.7% m/m vs 0.3% (core y/y 5.0%), with energy +10.8% m/m (gasoline +20.3%, roughly half the headline gain). Retail sales beat (+0.8% vs 0.3%) but gasoline did the work — the GDP-proxy control group ran just +0.1% vs 0.3% expected. Claims were 199K, inline. The regional surveys split: Empire State +25.5 (a big beat) against Philly Fed 20.9 (a miss, down from 37.8). Thread: this morning's edition said Bowman and Daly had talked the October hike down to ~31.6% and that PPI Thursday was the next verdict. The verdict came back hot — and didn't matter. What it means: breaks the mechanical 'hot data = more hike pricing' read. The market chose the risk-off tape over the inflation tape: Treasuries rallied, the 10-year fell to ~5.05-5.10% (a three-week low, ~27bp off Wednesday's 5.33% spike), DXY softened to ~102.03-102.07, and LSEG October pricing slipped to ~29%. MarketWatch's read: hot PPI is 'still not turning market in favor of an October rate hike.' The October question is no longer about the data — it's about the calendar (midterms) and whether anyone believes Warsh moves two weeks out. December (~90%+) is untouched.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Warsh speaks 10:30pm CT — the last Fed voice before Saturday's Oct 17 blackout (Hammack spoke 3:30pm CT; no verified readout had surfaced by NY close — her Monday 'rates need to move higher' stance is already priced). Friday 7:30am CT: import prices + housing starts; 8:15am CT: industrial production. September PCE lands Oct 29, after the meeting.

scenarios.base: October stays ~25-30% into the blackout; the meeting is priced as a hold and DXY chops 101.8-102.5.
scenarios.bear: A patient Warsh plus soft Friday data — October falls toward ~15% and DXY retests 101.5.
scenarios.bull: Warsh re-arms the hike — October back toward ~45% and DXY retests 102.75.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro rode the dollar fade to ~1.12 (+0.5%) even as its own data disappointed — eurozone IP missed and France CPI confirmed the energy overshoot.
chapters.meaning: What changed: EUR/USD rose ~0.5% to ~1.1216 in the US session, more than recovering the CPI-day selloff. The euro's own data was soft: eurozone industrial production fell 0.5% m/m in August vs flat consensus (July revised deeper to -0.3%), and France's final September CPI confirmed the overshoot (HICP 3.4% y/y, highest since January 2024 — energy did the work). The EU summit's second day wrapped with no cohesion headline surfacing. Thread: this morning's edition said the pair trades the Fed leg, not the ECB leg — the ECB's own chorus (Simkus: 'additional evidence suggesting some tightening may be necessary') was the steadier leg. What it means: confirms the shape. Neither the soft factory print nor the inline France CPI moved the pair — this week's euro is a dollar story with a fiscal overhang. The €100B+ war-driven fossil import bill from the summit is the winter drag the ECB has to price around.
chapters.fx: What to watch: eurozone final CPI Friday 9am CT; US import prices + housing starts Friday 7:30am CT for the dollar leg; France's revenue-section vote Oct 20 and Moody's Oct 23.
numbers: France HICP 3.4% y/y final (highest since Jan 2024); ECB Oct 29 hike ~12%

scenarios.bear: A hawkish Warsh re-fires October — 1.115 retests and the record EUR shorts (-99,332) stay loaded.
scenarios.bull: Soft Friday US data — the record-shorts squeeze runs toward 1.13.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling rode the dollar fade to ~1.323-1.324 (+0.4%) as a Reuters poll showed 54 of 63 economists expect the November hike — while Pill said it 'need not be the start of a long series.'
chapters.meaning: What changed: GBP/USD gained ~0.4% to ~1.3230-1.3242, recovering intraday to 1.3270 from the post-CPI low of 1.3137. The November-hike case got poll confirmation: 54 of 63 economists surveyed Oct 12-14 expect 25bp to 4.00% at the November meeting — but no majority expects more after that (30 of 61 see one more in Q1 2027, vs markets pricing four by Sep 2027). Pill, on day two, said a hike 'need not be the start of a long series' while warning catch-up wage dynamics need 'a prolonged period of restriction' — hawkish on inflation, dovish on pace, exactly Wednesday's framing. Bailey spoke (2nd of 4) with no verified new line. Thread: this morning said the GDP beat (+0.1%) covered the growth leg of the November case while Pill capped the 2027 path. What it means: confirms — near-certainty November (~86%+) with a capped path; economists sit between Pill and the market.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bailey Friday 2am CT (3rd of 4); UK retail sales Friday 1am CT; the Oct 28 budget; BoE decision Nov 5.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: USD/JPY faded to ~157.6-157.9 with the 10-year as Koeda warned against getting 'overly cautious' on hikes — but the franc, not the yen, was Thursday's haven.
chapters.meaning: What changed: USD/JPY slipped ~0.2% to ~157.64-157.93 as the 10-year fell to its three-week low — the pair is still breathing with the US yield leg. The BoJ side got a hawkish voice: board member Koeda said the bank should not get 'overly cautious' on rate hikes and put the neutral rate 'considerably above 1%' — upside inflation risks from AI demand, Middle East tensions, and the weak yen feeding raw-material costs. Thread: this morning said the BoJ side is frozen in the December-not-October shape and that last night proved the haven bid still isn't independent. What it means: confirms both — Koeda keeps December (>80%) alive with October (~9%) unchanged, and the haven ladder put the yen second: +0.34% vs the dollar against the franc's +0.59% (CHF/JPY +0.36%). When the fear is financial (AI debt) rather than purely geopolitical, Europe's haven out-bids Japan's.
chapters.fx: What to watch: US import prices + housing starts Friday for the yield leg; BoJ Oct 29-30 — the forecasts decide whether machinery orders (+5.2% beat) or industrial output (-2.4%) matters.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The haven finally showed up: USD/CHF fell ~0.57% to ~0.83 — Thursday's best G10 performer vs the dollar — while Swiss PPI missed and kept December cut risk on the table.
chapters.meaning: What changed: USD/CHF dropped ~0.5-0.57% to ~0.831, the strongest G10 move against the dollar on the board (tradingkey's cross table). The franc outperformed the yen on the same risk-off tape (CHF/JPY +0.36%) — the haven bid picked Europe over Japan. Switzerland's own print was soft: PPI +0.3% m/m vs 0.6% expected (BFS official) — pipeline pressures stay soft, which keeps December SNB cut risk on the table with the bank pinned at 0.00%. Schlegel's 11:30pm CT remarks produced no verified readout. Thread: this morning's edition said the franc slept through a genuine risk-off night and only moves on a verified shock or de-escalation. What it means: breaks the sleeping thesis — the franc woke up, and the pattern is instructive: when the fear is AI-debt and credit stress (CoreWeave bonds above 16%), the haven flow goes to the franc first, gold second, yen third. The dollar fade did half the work; the fear bid did the rest.
chapters.fx: What to watch: EUR/CHF as the contagion gauge; Trump's Saturday-evening Hormuz deadline; SNB Dec 10.
numbers: USD/CHF ~0.831 (-0.57% — best G10 vs the dollar Thursday)

scenarios.bear: Verified de-escalation — the fear premium clears and USD/CHF drifts back up.
scenarios.bull: A verified supply shock or a Saturday-deadline strike — the haven bid extends.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The aussie was the only G10 currency to fall against the dollar Thursday (-0.48% to ~0.6939): the jobs miss plus a risk-off tape is the worst possible combination for a risk proxy.
chapters.meaning: What changed: AUD/USD slipped ~0.48% to ~0.6939 — the lone loser on tradingkey's cross table as every other G10 currency gained on the dollar. The September jobs miss (-39,300 vs +20,000 expected; unemployment to a five-year high of 4.7%, above the RBA's 4.5% Q4 forecast) collided with a risk-off tape (Nasdaq's fourth straight down day, Asian equities routed overnight). Thread: this morning said the jobs miss broke the improving-AUD shape and the $0.70 test moved further away, with the record-shorts squeeze (-98,588, ~2nd percentile) needing the RBA to look through the miss. What it means: confirms — and deepens. November-hike odds pared further from the ~33% priced pre-print. The squeeze setup is still loaded, but it now needs two things: soft US data and an RBA willing to hike through labor slack. The risk-proxy leg of the aussie did the damage today; the policy leg is on trial until Nov 2-3.
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBA's Kent speaks Saturday; China Q3 GDP Monday; US import prices + IP Friday; RBA Nov 2-3 is the verdict.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The tug-of-war's legs pushed opposite ways: the EIA confirmed a -8.6M-barrel draw and WTI rallied +2.7% while the dollar leg faded — the loonie firmed gently to ~1.42.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the EIA confirmed the API draw — crude stocks fell 8.6M barrels (vs +0.2M expected) to 415.6M, 3% below the five-year average; total commercial petroleum stocks fell 13.4M. December WTI rallied 2.7% to $96.42 while December Brent sat ~$106.10 little changed — the Brent-WTI spread compressed to ~$9.7 from ~$10.5. Phil Flynn's read: easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions would be 'more negative for Brent than WTI' — the freight premium sits in Brent. Canada's factory sales beat (+1.5% vs 1.1%) but volumes were flat — prices did all the work. USD/CAD firmed gently to ~1.42 (-0.18%). Thread: this morning said both tug-of-war legs eased in tandem (sanctions-easing talk + dollar fade) and the 1.41-1.43 chop holds until one side wins. What it means: confirms the draw thesis — the gap decides direction, oil decides magnitude, and today they pushed opposite ways (tight physical + soft dollar = loonie firming). The 1.4299 52-week high is still the line in the sand.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Macklem speaks 11:15pm CT tonight; BoC's Alexopoulos Friday; Canada housing starts Friday 7:30am CT; US data Friday; a break of 1.4299 opens 1.44.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi drifted +0.2% to ~0.5616 on the dollar fade while RBNZ's Conway confirmed the two-way bet: October 28 is 'wide open,' but the direction is 'most likely up.'
chapters.meaning: What changed: NZD/USD added ~0.2% to ~0.5616 on the dollar fade, still hovering just above its 52-week low (0.5580). The RBNZ's chief economist Paul Conway (IMF sidelines, Bangkok) said the Oct 28 decision is 'wide open' — policymakers want flexibility to hold or hike 25bp — but the direction of the OCR is 'most likely up': oil gains plus a weaker NZD are adding near-term inflation pressure, though the board still expects inflation back inside 1-3% next year. Thread: this morning said the RBNZ sits at 2.75% with October 28 a genuine two-way bet (~50% priced) and NZ CPI Oct 21 the settler. What it means: confirms the shape — Conway validated the two-way framing and leaned it hawkish at the margin. Tonight's BusinessNZ PMI and food prices are texture; the CPI on Oct 21 is the verdict.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: The EIA confirmed the draw (-8.6M barrels): WTI rallied +2.7% to $96.42 while Brent lagged — the spread compressed to ~$9.7 as the freight premium, not demand, is what's priced.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the official EIA report confirmed the API's huge draw — crude stocks -8.6M barrels (vs +0.2M expected) to 415.6M, 3% below the five-year average; gasoline built 3.5M, distillates drew 2.5M (12% below seasonal norms), total commercial stocks -13.4M. December WTI gained 2.7% to $96.42 (WSJ live card, 12:10pm CT) while December Brent sat ~$106.10 little changed — the spread compressed from ~$10.5 to ~$9.7. The shadow-fleet sanctions-easing talk (a consideration, not an action) leaked Brent's freight premium; Phil Flynn's note that easing would be 'more negative for Brent than WTI' explains the divergence — the elevated freight cost lives in Brent's price. Fresh US sanctions on Iran (16 individuals, 10 entities) kept the escalatory lane open, and CNN reported new US strike plans including a MOAB option — planning, not an order. Thread: this morning said Brent $104-108 holds until a verified shock or ceasefire, the API draw was ignored, and EIA 11am CT was the confirmation test. What it means: confirms the range thesis — physical tightness (the draw) under the war premium re-bid WTI and unwound part of Brent's freight premium, but didn't break the range. The spread says the premium is still shipping risk, not demand.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Trump's Saturday-evening Hormuz deadline; any US/CENTCOM response; whether shadow-fleet easing talk becomes action; spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: The anti-dollar bid re-armed: gold ran to ~$4,150-4,175 (+1.5%+, futures $4,181 +1.8%) as the rate leg collapsed — the haven that works when FX havens hesitate.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold's bounce became a rally — spot ~$4,150-4,175 (+1.5% or more on the day), futures +1.79% to $4,181.30, as the 10-year fell to its three-week low and October-hike pricing kept fading. The defensive rotation fed it too: healthcare +2.6%, consumer staples +1%, while the Nasdaq fell a fourth straight day and the semiconductor index dropped an eighth straight session. Thread: this morning's edition said CPI day was the both-engines moment and the rate leg won (gold closed -1.66% at $4,107.90); the overnight ease re-armed the anti-dollar bid. What it means: confirms the two-engine model in both directions — the rate leg easing re-arms gold, the fear leg (AI debt, CoreWeave bonds above 16%, crypto liquidations near $1B) bids it. Gold is the haven that works when FX havens hesitate: CHF +0.59%, JPY +0.34%, gold +1.8%. The morning's map holds — capped by real yields while October stays priced, re-arming toward $4,300 if Friday's data collapses the repricing.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Warsh 10:30pm CT; US import prices + housing starts + IP Friday; the 10-year (~5.05-5.10%) is the cap to watch.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100-4,175 under the rate cap; direction comes from Friday's data.
scenarios.bear: A hawkish Warsh re-fires October — real yields jump again and gold slides back toward $4,000.
scenarios.bull: Soft Friday data collapses the repricing — gold re-arms toward $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
